# Research Brief

## When to Use
- Starting a new design research effort (discovery, generative, or evaluative)
- Aligning stakeholders on what questions the research will and will not answer
- Scoping participant recruitment before user interviews or usability tests

## Procedure

### 1. Understand the Design Challenge

Read the task description carefully. Identify:
- The product or feature under investigation
- The user problem or business question driving the research
- Any known assumptions or hypotheses the team holds
- Constraints (timeline, participant access, budget)

### 2. Define Research Goals

Write 2–4 goal statements using the format:
> "To understand [phenomenon] so that [design decision] can be made."

Each goal must be tied to a specific design decision — not just general learning.

### 3. Write Research Questions

For each goal, write 2–3 open-ended research questions. Good research questions:
- Begin with "How", "What", "Why", or "In what ways"
- Cannot be answered with yes/no
- Address user behaviour, mental models, or context — not preferences alone

### 4. Select Research Methods

Choose 1–3 methods appropriate to the goals:
- **Generative**: Semi-structured interviews, diary studies, contextual inquiry
- **Evaluative**: Usability testing, cognitive walkthrough, heuristic evaluation
- **Desk research**: Competitive analysis, literature review, analytics review

Justify each method choice against the research questions.

### 5. Define Participant Profile

Specify:
- User segment (role, context of use, product familiarity)
- Screening criteria (include/exclude)
- Recommended number of participants per method (typical: 5–8 for qualitative)
- Recruitment approach

### 6. Set Success Criteria

Define what "done" looks like:
- Specific insights the team needs to unblock design decisions
- Minimum confidence threshold (e.g., "pattern confirmed across at least 4 participants")
- Decisions that will be made once research is complete

### 7. Write the Brief

Save to `research/research-brief.md` using this structure:

```
# Research Brief: {Product/Feature}

## Background
## Research Goals
## Research Questions
## Methods
## Participant Profile
## Timeline
## Success Criteria
## Out of Scope
```

All sections must be filled. "Out of Scope" must list at least 2 explicit exclusions so stakeholders know what the research will not cover.
